items.stem: Which layer of the Earth is the thin, solid, outermost layer we live on?

options.rationale: Correct: the crust is the thin, solid outer layer.
The inner core is the deepest, solid metal centre.
The mantle lies below the crust and is mostly solid but can flow slowly.
The outer core is a deep liquid metal layer.

items.explanation: Correct: the crust is the thin, solid outer layer.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Earthquakes and volcanoes mostly occur in the same belts. What best explains this? (Select ONE)

options.text: Both are concentrated at the boundaries between tectonic plates
options.rationale: Correct: plate boundaries are where most quakes and volcanoes occur.

options.text: They happen randomly with no pattern
They only occur in the middle of flat plates
options.rationale: Most occur at boundaries, not plate interiors.

options.text: Volcanoes cause the plates to first appear
options.rationale: Plates are not created by volcanoes in this way.

items.explanation: Correct: plate boundaries are where most quakes and volcanoes occur.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Select TWO features typical of a composite (stratovolcano) eruption. (Select TWO)

options.rationale: Correct: composite volcanoes often erupt explosively with ash.

options.text: Steep sides built from layers of ash and lava
options.rationale: Correct: alternating layers build their steep cones.

options.text: Very gentle, runny lava forming a broad flat shield
options.rationale: That describes shield volcanoes, not composite ones.

options.text: No connection to any plate boundary
options.rationale: Composite volcanoes are typically at convergent boundaries.

items.explanation: Correct: composite volcanoes often erupt explosively with ash.
